newsitem.title: MALI: Mali opposition plans marches to back poll boycott.
newsitem.headline: Mali opposition plans marches to back poll boycott.

text.p: Mali's 18-party radical opposition plans to stage a series of marches led by women militants to reinforce its boycott of Sunday's rerun parliamentary election, opposition officials say.
The programme, published as part of its campaign against the government election timetable, begins with marches on Thursday and culminates in nationwide marches on election day itself.

The government of President Alpha Oumar Konare has not formally banned protests but informed sources say that mixed patrols of police and gendarmes will take strict measures to ensure security on polling day.
Witnesses say that such patrols, which deliberately exclude members of the army, have already stepped up nighttime patrols and identity checks.
Mali was widely praised for its 1992 transition from Moussa Traore's dictatorship to a multi-party system.
The former French colony's constitutional court scrapped an April 13 parliamentary poll citing organisational chaos.
The opposition wanted the whole election timetable revised but Konare pressed ahead with a May 11 presidential election, won the backing of the court for that and then the election.

Almost 600 candidates are due to stand for Mali's 147 national assembly seats on Sunday. Konare's Alliance for Democracy in Mali (ADEMA), 18 other parties and 13 independent lists will contest the election.
